name: GHRP-3

lead: GHRP-3 is one of a numbered family of synthetic peptides that stimulate growth hormone release. Physique enthusiasts discuss it as a way to raise GH and IGF-1 for more muscle and less fat.

The chain runs from growth hormone release to higher GH and IGF-1 to more muscle and leanness. Like other GHRPs, it is classed as an agonist of the ghrelin/growth hormone secretagogue receptor. Published work on it is mostly analytical chemistry for doping control; no completed human trial was found.

paras: It is used in research-peptide routines in physique communities, usually alongside training and diet. It is much less documented than better-known secretagogues.
No safety data from human trials were found. It is named on the World Anti-Doping Agency prohibited list and is not an approved medicine.

angle.text: GHRP-3 is one of the numbered growth hormone-releasing peptides, discussed by physique enthusiasts as a way to raise GH for muscle and leanness. It is mostly known from anti-doping literature; human training or appearance trials have not been reported.

lead: GHRP-3 is a synthetic growth hormone-releasing peptide (GHRP), one of a numbered series of small peptides that act on the ghrelin/growth hormone secretagogue receptor to stimulate growth hormone release.[1] It is listed by name among the peptides prohibited by the World Anti-Doping Agency.[2]
The published literature on GHRP-3 specifically is very thin. It appears mainly in anti-doping analytical chemistry papers, and no completed human trial was found.

paras: Growth hormone secretagogues act on the ghrelin/GH secretagogue receptor (GHSR) or the GHRH receptor, and many also raise IGF-1, prolactin and cortisol. The Wikipedia overview lists GHRP-3 only as a GHSR agonist, without further detail on its development.[1]

Anti-doping laboratories have published methods for detecting GHRP-1 through GHRP-6 and related peptides in urine, and studies of in vitro metabolites of prohibited peptides have included this class.[2][3] The relevant papers describe GHRPs as small peptides that raise endogenous growth hormone and were developed with performance enhancement in mind.

No studies found. One registered phase 1/2 trial of continuous GHRP-3 infusion, examining the growth hormone-IGF-I system, blood pressure, glucose and insulin resistance, was withdrawn before enrolment.[4]
